rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill, recognized by its front matter (`name: habeas`), so `requirements.cli.skill_conventions` applies to it as a site.

The requirement has one obligation for each site: the description MUST state when to use the skill in terms of the user's task. The `description` in `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` begins "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". It then lists concrete signals of such a project: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references. This says when to use the skill, and it does so in terms of the user's work. It also adds that the skill is the reference for directive and reference syntax, `habeas status`/`habeas info`, and common gotchas.

The description names other bundled skills (`habeas-requirements`, `habeas-refactor`, `habeas-evidence`, `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`) as the ones to pick for particular tasks. The requirement's MAY allows this, and it imposes nothing to check. No violation matches were listed for this site, and I found no gap.

text: Each bundled skill's description MUST state when to use it in terms of the user's task. It MAY name another bundled skill to use instead where an agent could confuse the two. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
